title: Environmental Systems Engineering, Minor (College of Earth and Mineral Sciences)
notes: 18cr exact bulletin match on the nominal course list, computed 37cr against CMPSC after a real hidden-prereq chain. Pairs name-for-name with the already-built Environmental Systems Engineering major (code ENVSYS), which already requires every one of these exact courses. Prescribed Courses (15cr, all required, no choice): MNPR 301 + ENVSE 406 (ENVSE 406 has a real same-term concurrent requirement on MNPR 301 -- both listed here, MNPR 301 first) + EME 460 (prereq-free) + ENVSE 450 (needs CHEM 110) + ENVSE 427 (a genuine 5-branch AND chain: CHEM 110 AND CHEM 112 AND MATH 141 AND MNPR 301 AND [CE 360 or EME 303] -- picked EME 303 over CE 360 since EME 303's own chain [MATH 250/251 + PHYS 211] is shallower than CE 360's [EMCH 212, itself needing EMCH 210/211 + MATH 141]). Elective (select 1 of 3, 3cr): picked ENVSE 400 over EGEE 470 (needs EME 301, an unrelated and deeper chain) and MNPR 426 (also needs EME 301/MATSE 401) -- ENVSE 400 needs only CHEM 110 + PHYS 211 (already required by CMPSC) + MATH 141 (already required by CMPSC), reusing the CHEM 110 already forced by the prescribed courses above with zero net-new codes. Real hidden-prereq chain against CMPSC: CHEM 110 needs MATH 22, which needs MATH 21 (the same MATH-21-chain pattern documented repeatedly across this project, e.g. MICRBMIN/EBFMIN/REBPMIN/ENGYMIN); CHEM 112 needs CHEM 110; EME 303 needs MATH 250/251 (added MATH 251, needs only MATH 141, already present) + PHYS 211 (already present). Added CHEM 110 + CHEM 112 + MATH 22 + MATH 21 + EME 303 + MATH 251 explicitly (19cr) for the CMPSC pairing; the ENVSYS major's own flowchart already includes every one of these codes (CHEM 110/111/112, EME 301/303/460, MATH 21/22/140/141/251, PHYS 211/212, and all of ENVSE 400/406/427/450 plus MNPR 301) on its own semester plan, so the entire addition collapses to a no-op against ENVSYS itself. Computed total against CMPSC: 18 (nominal) + 19 (hidden chain) = 37cr.
